title: Averaging randomized norm bounds
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on its outcome space, and let $q>0$. If, for every $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, the $q$-moment norm of the randomized expansion $R_rf$ is at most the $q$-moment norm of $g$, then the norm obtained by averaging $|R_rf(x)|^q$ over both $x$ under $P$ and uniform $r$ is at most the $q$-moment norm of $g$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive atom masses
$f,g$ are real-valued functions on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $q>0$. If $\|R_rf\|_{q,P}\le\|g\|_{q,P}$ for every sign vector $r$, then $(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|R_rf(x)|^q)^{1/q}\le\|g\|_{q,P}$, with uniform signs $r$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$; $R_rh=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\chi_S(r)h_S$.
